description: We are TRU Computer Science students exploring the use of applied computer science and coding in topics surrounding aerospace, environmental studies, and the community.
summary:
Application is built for small communities frequently at risk from wildfires by helping identify common hotspot trends throughout the year. It addresses the challenge by harmonizing 2018–2025 Canadian MODIS and VIIRS data onto one consistent data set.
Used to guide evacuation efforts, and improve fire response in places lacking rescue and modern alert systems
details:
This project solves a measurement discrepancy in NASA wildfire monitoring. The application harmonizes 2018–2025 Canadian MODIS and VIIRS detections onto one consistent scale and serves an interactive map, analytics charts, summary metrics, activity calendar, and CSV export filtered by year, month, and searched location. It works by using a api to fetch live data from a spatially indexed database featuring the harmonized data sets.

Coding tools we used include react, flask api, mapboxgljs, duckdb, vit. The IDEs we used were Pycharm and VS code. The language we used was Python 3 and JavaScript.

One factor we considered was our target audience. We developed the website UI to be easily understandable, and used inclusive color ramps and fonts to increase usability.
